name: IRF520
description: N-channel power MOSFET in TO-220, 100V / 9.2A, Rds(on) 0.27 ohm at Vgs=10V. Standard-threshold (not logic-level). Lead order G-D-S, tab is drain. Familiar as the through-hole part on the cheap 'IRF520 MOSFET module', though its 4V threshold and 0.27 ohm make it mediocre for direct 5V/3.3V logic drive.

TO-220.notes: TO-220AB, label toward you, leads down: G-D-S. The tab is the drain (electrically live). Datasheet figure shows the N-channel symbol and leads labeled S/D/G; the 1-2-3 order is the universal IR-lineage assignment, identical to irf540/irfz44.

typical_application: Low-side DC switching of motors, heaters, LED strings and small loads up to ~100V. Drive the gate to 10V for the rated Rds(on); add a gate resistor (~10-100 ohm) and a pulldown so the gate does not float on.
gotchas: NOT logic-level: Vgs(th) is 2-4V and full turn-on wants ~10V, so a bare 5V/3.3V pin leaves it half-on and hot. The popular 'IRF520 module' has exactly this flaw for microcontroller PWM -- use a logic-level MOSFET (IRLZ44N, IRL540) or a gate driver instead
modest ratings for a power MOSFET: 9.2A and 0.27 ohm mean more heat than an IRFZ44/IRF540 at the same current
tab is the drain and electrically live; isolate it from grounded heatsinks
add a flyback diode across inductive loads (the body diode is slow)
IRF520N is the improved-process successor (lower typical Rds(on)) with the identical TO-220 G-D-S pinout and tab=drain
